title: A table fits its columns to the box before it pans
body:
coax lays a table out at 1000 columns (`TABLE_WIDTH`, used in `kept_whole` in `src/ui.rs`), so a cell never wraps. A table wider than the box pans sideways. A table that fits is laid out at the box width with the prose. One long cell is enough to make a table pan.

cmr can wrap cells. Its `table` function in `lib.rs` takes a target width. It narrows the widest column one column at a time until the table fits, and wraps each cell's words to its column. When a column would go below 8 (`MIN_COLUMN`), cmr draws each row as `header: value` lines instead.

## Proposal

- No column is laid out wider than 40 cells, even when the box has room. A longer cell wraps.
- A table still wider than the box is narrowed, widest column first. A column stops at 16 cells, or at its natural width when that is less.
- A table still too wide with every column at that floor pans as it does now. It never stacks.

cmr needs no change for this. When cmr narrows the widest column first to a target width, each column ends at the smaller of its natural width and one common level. A cap gives the same widths. So coax works out one target width from the natural column widths, the cap and the floor, and lays the table out at it. The floor is above `MIN_COLUMN`, so cmr never stacks. coax reads the natural column widths from the rule row of the table laid out at `TABLE_WIDTH`.

## Out of scope

- A wrap and pan toggle on a table, in coax-a03507.

## Open

- The cap and the floor are first guesses. They need tuning on real agent tables.
- cmr breaks a word longer than its column partway through, so a long path in a cell splits. A column could widen to fit its longest word, up to a hard limit. One target width cannot give one column a higher floor than the rest, so that needs a change to cmr's `table`.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/85c47808
notes.text:
Done in the working tree on `dev`, not yet committed. `table_width` and `column_widths` in `src/ui.rs` set the width a table is laid out at, with `COLUMN_CAP` at 40 and `COLUMN_FLOOR` at 16. The code uses both for a table that fits the box and for one that pans. `column_widths` reads the rule row of the table laid out at `TABLE_WIDTH`, after trimming the padding `cmr::layout` adds to every row.

At 100 columns, a two-column table with a paragraph in one cell wraps inside the box. A five-column table at 105 natural columns narrows to fit. A seven-column table drops each column to 16 and pans. A `code` path in a 16-cell column breaks partway through, as the Open item says.

The test `a_link_in_a_panned_table_is_hovered_and_clicked_on_the_columns_it_shows` in `src/app.rs` built its wide table from one 60-character cell, which now wraps. It now uses four columns.
